plan.title: Treated vs control DE adjusted for sex and age
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is which genes differ between treated and control in a 12-sample human adipose bulk RNA-seq cohort (12,000 genes, Salmon-derived gene-level counts), where the two groups are unpaired and NOT matched on age, and sex (F/M) and age (years) vary across subjects. Because age distribution differs between the groups, an unadjusted comparison would confound treatment with age; sex likewise cannot be ignored. The plan therefore fits a single negative-binomial GLM per gene with design ~ condition + sex + age: the condition term estimates the treatment effect adjusted for both covariates, per rule R-0023 (covariates as design terms, never regressed out of the counts). DESeq2 is the primary test (Wald, apeglm-shrunk LFC) and edgeR quasi-likelihood is run on the identical design as the second method; the intersection of the two gene sets is reported as the high-confidence set per R-0042, since at 6 vs 6 replicates the two tools each call genes the other misses. QC precedes the model: blind vst PCA and sample distances to catch an outlier or batch-like structure, plus an explicit tabulation of age and sex imbalance between the groups so the covariate adjustment is grounded in the actual imbalance. With only 12 samples and 4 design parameters, residual df = 8, so power is limited and this is stated in the report rather than hidden. No enrichment step is planned: the research question asks only which genes differ, and pathway work was not requested.
